narrative.overview: OSRS Tracker is a cool, flat market terminal. The ground is a deliberately un-warm graphite (#0e0f12) — slate, not stone — carrying near-white type on hairline structure. There are no bevels, no glow, no gradients-as-decoration and no gold: the owner read every warm/parchment/carved-stone treatment as "AI slop" and rejected it. What remains is a quiet, dense surface where the only color is a single flat signal — green means gain, red means loss — and everything else is modelled in weight, scale and a 1px line. The system runs on one accent economy. Green (#27e07a) is the live, positive signal; red (#ff5c5c) is the only second voice, reserved for loss. There is no third hue, no blue, no status palette, no decorative tint. Depth is not expressed by shadow — surfaces are flat panels edged by hairlines, and elevation reads as a change of ground tone (#0e0f12 → #15171b → #1a1d22), never as a floating card. The voice is blunt and the surface is instrumental. Nothing is ornamental, nothing floats, nothing fades up. The accent is scarce enough that when a figure turns full green it carries meaning — a real, fillable profit — rather than decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Cool graphite ground (#0e0f12), deliberately not warm; recessed and raised tones layer without shadow.
One flat signal accent: green = gain, red = loss. No gold, no third hue, no status palette.
1px hairline borders carry all structure; surfaces are flat, never floated on a grey shadow.
Hierarchy from weight and scale, not uppercase tracking, color noise or ornament.
Geist for everything typeset; Geist Mono for every market figure (tabular-nums). Soft-square 10px corners.

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Color is spent only as signal: green for gain, red for loss. Nothing else on the screen carries a hue — no blue, no gold, no tinted panels, no decorative accent. Everything else is graphite, hairline and near-white, and emphasis is bought with weight and scale, never with color.

rules.name: The Lit-Means-Liquid Rule
rules.body: A profit figure shows full Signal Green (#27e07a, .pos.lit) only when it is both real and liquid/fillable; a positive-but-unproven profit stays Dim Green (#1c7d4b, .pos); a loss is red (.neg). Full green is a claim about fillability, not merely about sign.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Decoration Rule
rules.body: Emphasis comes from weight (500/600) and scale, not from uppercase tracking, color or ornament. There is no all-caps eyebrow device: labels are quiet mono at letter-spacing 0, and a heading is never preceded by a tracked-out kicker.

rules.name: The Tabular-Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number sourced from the market feed is set in Geist Mono with tabular-nums. Figures never use the sans UI face; prose never uses the mono.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest and separated by a 1px hairline, never by a shadow. A soft grey drop-shadow under a card is forbidden; if two surfaces must read apart, change the ground tone or draw a hairline. Shadows appear only as a focus ring, an accent ring, or a transient tooltip.

dos: Do keep the ground cool graphite (#0e0f12) and layer depth with tone (#0a0b0d → #15171b → #1a1d22), not shadow.
Do spend color only as signal: Signal Green (#27e07a) for gain, Loss Red (#ff5c5c) for loss, nothing else.
Do reserve full Signal Green for a profit that is real AND liquid (the Lit-Means-Liquid Rule); keep unproven profit Dim Green (#1c7d4b).
Do draw structure with 1px hairlines (#22262b / #2f343b) and keep surfaces flat.
Do set every market figure in Geist Mono with tabular-nums; buy emphasis with weight and scale.
Do keep corners soft-square (10px panels / 7px controls) and borders 1px.
donts: Don't reintroduce warm/fantasy dressing — no gold, parchment, wood, carved-stone, coin-gold or glow. The owner rejected these as "AI slop".
Don't add a third hue — no blue, no status palette, no decorative tint. Green already means up, red means down.
Don't float a surface on a soft grey drop-shadow; separate surfaces with tone or a hairline.
Don't use bevels, inner-light modelling, or gradient-filled text; emphasis is weight, scale and the flat accent.
Don't put an all-caps / tracked-out eyebrow or kicker above a heading. Labels are quiet mono at letter-spacing 0.
Don't use pills, large radii, or organic curves; the form language is restrained soft-square.
